title: Exactly One Consecutive Set Bits Pair
summary: Given an integer n, determine if its binary representation contains exactly one pair of consecutive set bits, and return true if so, otherwise return false.
statement: Given an integer n, determine if its binary representation contains exactly one pair of consecutive set bits, and return true if so, otherwise return false.
constraints: Inspect adjacent positions in the binary representation of positive n.
Count each occurrence of the substring 11, including overlapping occurrences.
Return true only when the count is exactly one.
hints: Write n in binary without the 0b prefix.
Each adjacent set-bit pair appears as substring 11.
Use a substring count that includes the relevant starts.
Require the final count to equal one, not merely be positive.
editorial: Require the final count to equal one, not merely be positive.

tests.explanation: Six is binary 110, which contains exactly one adjacent 11 pair.
Seven is binary 111, whose two overlapping 11 pairs make it invalid.
